summary: Macro backdrop for ags: mixed (score -1 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates +; dollar 0; brl −; risk 0; energy +; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Cheese +16.3%; weakest: Lean hogs -16.8%. Key releases ahead: US Congressional Elections (11-03 10:16 AM ET); US Average Hourly Earnings m/m (11-06 8:30 AM ET); US Non-Farm Employment Change (11-06 8:30 AM ET); US Unemployment Rate (11-06 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.94% (-35 bp in a month), 2-year 4.56% (-32 bp); 2s10s curve +38 bp (-3 bp in a month). Falling yields ease funding costs and support commodity investment flows. T-bill yield 3.99% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.69 (-0.2% in a month, +3.5% YTD). USD/BRL 5.437 (+4.1% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.637 (-1.0%); USD/MXN 18.55 (+1.3%).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -1.3% in a month (+11.4% YTD); VIX 18.8. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 96.40 $/bbl (+7.8% in a month), Brent 104.47, ULSD 4.446 $/gal (+2.0%), natural gas 2.91 (-13.0%). Higher crude lifts biofuel margins (soybean oil, corn for ethanol) and synthetic-fibre costs (supports cotton), but raises diesel, drying and freight costs. Natural gas drives nitrogen fertilizer costs for next year's corn.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper +0.3% in a month, Shanghai Composite -5.3%, Hang Seng -2.4%, yuan +1.0% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 9 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (27%); S&P GSCI -0.6% in a month; gold -4.5%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
